title: Retail Sales Performance Report: 2023–2024
executive_summary: Across 520 cleaned orders, the business generated $445,325 in total revenue over 2023–2024, with a healthy 10.1% year-over-year increase from 2023 to 2024. The East region led all regions in revenue. Within 2024, revenue accelerated through Q3 before a modest Q4 dip. High-discount Electronics orders represent a notable revenue concentration risk, and the order revenue distribution is highly right-skewed, indicating a small number of large orders drive a disproportionate share of total revenue.

key_findings.statement: Total revenue across all 520 orders was $445,325.09, yielding an average order value of $856.39.
The East region generated the highest revenue at $130,516.69, followed by North ($124,845.75), West ($99,428.16), and South ($90,534.49).
2024 quarterly revenue showed consistent growth through Q3: Q1 $36,108.31, Q2 $56,616.79, Q3 $71,674.99, then a slight decline in Q4 to $68,948.71. Q3 was the strongest quarter.
Revenue grew from $211,976.29 in 2023 to $233,348.80 in 2024, a year-over-year increase of 10.1%.
Among Electronics orders with a discount of 20% or more, there were 22 orders totalling $50,035.33 in revenue — representing 11.2% of total revenue.

Order revenue is highly right-skewed: mean $856.39, median $313.28, standard deviation $1,295.74, ranging from $5.27 to $7,844.02. The large gap between mean and median indicates a small number of high-value orders significantly inflate the average.
There are 222 unique customers. The single highest-revenue customer contributed $27,793.13, representing 6.2% of total revenue — a meaningful concentration for one customer out of 222.

limitations: The dataset covers only 520 orders; findings may not be representative of the full customer or product population if the export was a sample.
Discount percentages are taken at face value from the raw export; any data entry errors in discount_pct would affect the high-discount Electronics filter.
Customer concentration analysis identifies the top customer by revenue share but does not account for order frequency or profitability, which could alter the risk assessment.
Quarterly 2024 trends cannot be compared directly to 2023 quarterly data as those breakdowns were not computed, limiting seasonality analysis.
No product-level margin data is available, so revenue figures do not reflect profitability.
conclusion: The business delivered solid growth in 2023–2024, with total revenue of $445,325 and a 10.1% year-over-year increase. The East and North regions are the primary revenue drivers. Within 2024, momentum built through Q3 with a slight Q4 softening. High-discount Electronics orders warrant monitoring given their 11.2% revenue share. The highly skewed order distribution and 6.2% single-customer revenue concentration suggest opportunities to broaden the customer base and reduce dependency on a small number of large transactions.
